Evidence: Exposing overreach, Partisan mobilization, Electoral weapon
#Aletheia #DOJ #USPol

The article claims to expose dangerous federal overreach to protect civil liberties and warn voters about the dangers of unchecked partisan power.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

The underlying report documents real White House pressure on the DOJ, but the article weaponizes this serious civil liberties issue for midterm mobilization.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.15, -0.35) — Deception

Verdict: CONDITIONAL — Revelation into Deception. The article reports on genuine, documented institutional overreach but dilutes its impact with highly partisan electoral fear-mongering.
Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.15, z: 1)

- DOJ Weaponization Report: PASS (0.60, -0.20) — Accurately reports White House pressure.
- Midterm Electoral Framing: FAIL (-0.70, -0.50) — Weaponizes overreach for votes.
A newly released report confirms the Biden White House pressured the DOJ to issue the 2021 Garland memo targeting parents at school board meetings despite constitutional concerns.

The Bright Side:
The article successfully highlights critical, documented evidence of executive overreach and the erosion of constitutional boundaries within federal law enforcement.
The Plane Error: Lyrical vs Historical (WHY vs CAUSE). The article uses the historical fact of DOJ overreach to justify a highly partisan, electoral narrative.

Social Physics Analysis:
The actors execute a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using the pretext of defending civil liberties to manufacture midterm panic and project all institutional corruption onto one party.

The Trajectory: The Path of Revelation into Deception.
When you map the gap between exposing government overreach and partisan electoral panic, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception.

The Unavoidable Truth: The White House pressured the DOJ to target protesting parents despite internal constitutional concerns.

The Unavoidable Lie: Only one political party weaponizes federal law enforcement to target political opponents.

Alethekanon:
Documented executive overreach is a grave threat to civil liberties, but reducing it to a partisan midterm campaign slogan dilutes the systemic accountability required.

Awwthekanon:
Parents should always feel safe speaking up for their children without fearing federal investigation. True accountability means protecting everyone's rights, not scoring points.

Brothekanon:
Bro, the White House pressuring the DOJ to target parents is definitely messed up. But using it to scare people into voting a certain way just feels like standard election spin.

"Woe to those who make unjust laws, to those who issue oppressive decrees." Isaiah 10:1 PASS
Using state power to suppress dissent is a timeless injustice, regardless of which party holds the gavel.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
New Report On Biden Targeting Parents Shows What Dems Will Do As Soon As They Gain Power

A Democrat-controlled Congress would give the same party subpoena power, committee leadership roles, and resources to do what it's done in the past: investigate and harass its opponents.

Actual Article Body:
A Democrat-controlled Congress would give the same party subpoena power, committee leadership roles, and resources to do what it’s done in the past: investigate and harass its opponents.

Sunday marked five years since then-Attorney General Merrick Garland issued a memorandum that instructed his Department of Justice (DOJ) to help investigate and prosecute parents who showed up at school board meetings to complain about far-left initiatives or Covid policies. Five years later we now know that the Biden White House was behind Garland’s effort to target parents, The Federalist’s Matt Kittle reported.

The anniversary and new finding also come on the heels of former Special Counsel Jack Smith’s testimony before Congress last week, in which his lawfare efforts to keep President Donald Trump out of office faced further scrutiny. With the midterms less than a month away, both instances serve to remind Americans of what Democrats will do with power given the chance: wage a lawfare campaign against their political opponents.

Back in September of 2021, the National School Boards Association (NSBA) sent a letter to the Biden administration asking it to take on the “immediate threat” that parents posed to their children’s schools. The “threat” stemmed from parents who were voicing their concerns and criticisms about critical race theory curriculum, mask mandates, and vaccine mandates. The NSBA wanted the Biden administration to treat the parents speaking out as “equivalent to a form of domestic terrorism.” Notably, the NSBA later apologized and acknowledged “there was no justification for some of the language included in the letter.”

Nonetheless, Garland had issued a memo entitled “Partnership Among Federal, State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Law Enforcement to Address Threats Against School Administrators, Board Members, Teachers, and Staff.” The memo instructed the FBI to meet with federal, state, and local law enforcement to focus on the alleged threats and how to respond to them. As a result of this memo, the federal government opened 25 preliminary assessment files regarding alleged “school board threats.”

In other words, a Democrat-led “justice” department decided that questioning or opposing left-wing thought orthodoxy like CRT justified the investigation of ordinary Americans with the intent of prosecution.

Nonetheless, the NSBA claimed that an independent review found that there was no collusion with the Biden administration. But a new report from the DOJ reveals, as Kittle put it, “the Biden White House was squarely behind Garland’s effort to find a federal ‘hook’ to prosecute parents and school policy protesters with federal crimes.”

According to the new report, DOJ senior officials and loyalists Biden put in place there “initially pushed back” on the NSBA’s request to target parents, “questioning the constitutionality of the request.” In fact, one email shows Kevin Chambers, then-associate deputy attorney general, calling the effort to enlist federal law enforcement and the claim that parents were domestic terrorists “ridiculous.” But the DOJ ultimately “moved ahead with issuing the Garland Memorandum based on pressure from Biden Administration officials in the White House and leadership at the Office of the Deputy Attorney General (‘ODAG’) at the Department of Justice.”

The Biden administration also coordinated with the NSBA on “talking points” to counter parents and other opponents of critical race theory and transgender ideology, Kittle reported.

In addition to these further revelations of Biden administration overreach, Special Counsel Jack Smith, an appointee of Garland, and the anti-Trump lawfare he led during the 2024 election cycle again took center stage last week. Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, revealed during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing that Smith obtained communications from more than a dozen media outlets, including those of The Federalist’s Editor-in-Chief Mollie Hemingway. Smith obtained the messages as part of his “Arctic Frost” witch hunt, which was an unconstitutional effort to get Trump that resulted in Smith’s team spying on members of Congress and the media.

Smith’s team also targeted nearly 5,000 Americans who made political donations to President Donald Trump, Grassley announced. One Iowan who donated $10 to the president just months before the 2020 election had his home address, bank information, and other personal information handed over to the Biden administration’s weaponized FBI and DOJ.

Democrats targeted parents who challenged what their children were being taught, journalists who scrutinized the Biden administration, and Americans who gave Trump as little as $10. They used regular acts of political participation as justification for government investigation and overreach. With each abuse of power, Democrats sent the American people a stark message: Speaking up or disagreeing with the narratives of the regime could put them on the government’s target list.

That’s the legacy voters need to remember this November. A Democrat-controlled Congress would give the same party subpoena power, committee leadership roles, and resources to do what it’s done in the past: investigate and harass its opponents. Democrats don’t need to get back into the White House to haul Americans before committees or demand their records. They just need Congress.
